messages:

Subject: Request for RCA and mitigation steps — May 20th service disruption

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the briefing last week. Durham's engineering leadership has asked for a concise RCA and the specific remediation steps we'll need to validate on our side. Specifically:
- A one-page summary we can share with compliance;
- A timeline of the events and ticket IDs;
- Owner-assigned action items and estimated delivery dates;

Can you please send a draft by Monday so we can review internally? Our SREs (sre@durhambank.com) will need the runbook changes to verify.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this affects our audit window.

Regards,
Alex
Alex Cooper
Director, Infrastructure — Durham Bank
From: ava.chen@redwood.com
To: Alex Cooper <alex.cooper@durhambank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Durham Bank post-incident RCA, timeline, and verification plan
Attachments: durham_rca_summary.pdf; may20-timeline.csv; remediation-runbook.md

Alex —

Thank you for the request and for the open call last week. Attached is our initial post-incident packet — it contains:

1) Executive summary (one page) — root cause in plain language and customer impact.
2) Annotated timeline (CSV) — events, service metrics, and the internal ticket references.
3) Mitigation and verification runbook (MD) — step-by-step checks your SREs can run.

Key points in brief:
- Root cause: an edge-case race in our prefix/KV cache eviction path exposed under a rare sequence of concurrent model warmups and autoscale events. This led to increased tokenization latency for ~18 minutes on 2027-05-20 between 15:07–15:25 UTC.
- Impact: ~7% of requests in your cluster experienced >2s tail latency; no data leakage or model correctness regression observed.
- Immediate mitigation: we deployed a guard that serializes cache evictions for concurrent warmup flows (rolled at 15:40 UTC).

Action items we propose (owners and ETA are in the attached runbook):
- Short-term: add a guarded eviction flag + metrics (owner: david.kim; ETA: 2027-06-21).
- Medium-term: stronger prefork/warmup coordination and better autoscale decoupling (owner: karthik.iyer; ETA: 2027-07-12).
- Long-term: compiler/kernel-level safeguard for quantized eviction paths (owner: infrastructure research; ETA: Q4 2027).

Please review the attachments with your SREs. If acceptable, we can schedule a verification window next week where we walk through the runbook with your team.

Note: we included the CSV timeline and a short one-page PDF you can provide to your compliance team.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Per Marissa's suggestions we updated the executive summary to include the exact UTC window and added rollback criteria and the JIRA ref.

Summary (TL;DR):
- What happened: a rare cache eviction race during concurrent model warmups caused temporary tokenization tail latency increases.
- When: 2027-05-20, 15:07–15:25 UTC (18 minutes).
- Impact on Durham: ~7% of requests hitting your reserved pool saw >2s tail latency; no request errors and no data exfiltration.
- Root cause: eviction logic did not account for in-flight KV references while multiple warmups triggered asynchronous eviction paths.
- Immediate fix: serialized eviction guard deployed at 15:40 UTC; metrics added to detect recurrence.

Action plan highlights (see attached runbook for full owners/ETAs):
1) Short-term (safe guard + metrics) — david.kim — ETA: 2027-06-21.
2) Medium-term (autoscale coordination) — karthik.iyer — ETA: 2027-07-12.
3) Verification window: propose Wed 2027-06-23 16:00–17:00 UTC for a run-through with your SREs. Please confirm if that works for Durham.

Attachments: the packet includes a one-page PDF you can share with compliance, the annotated CSV timeline, and the step-by-step runbook for verification.

If we agree on the verification window, we'll run tests with read-only traffic and walk through the metrics to confirm the guard behaves as intended.

Thanks — and sorry again for the disruption. We'll be monitoring your pool closely.

Best regards,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
